sentences.text: Moganopterus was a large pterosaur with a preserved skull length of about 95 cm and a longest preserved neck vertebra measuring 14.5 cm. Its skull is the largest known among all toothed pterosaurs. Based on its skull and neck size, Moganopterus had a wingspan of about 7 meters, making it one of the largest known ctenochasmatid pterosaurs.
The animal possessed very elongated jaws with straight edges and at least sixty-two teeth in its skull. The lower jaws of Moganopterus are 68.5 cm long and lack a keel.

A large rectangular opening called the fenestra nasoantorbitalis represents 22% of the snout length. A long and narrow parietal crest on the back of the skull sticks out at a 15° angle to the skull's longitudinal axis. Excluding the crest, the Moganopterus skull is 11.5 times longer than it is tall. The neck vertebrae of Moganopterus are five times longer than they are high.
Hollow structures reinforced by struts are present in the parietal crest and vertebrae of Moganopterus. The fourth cervical vertebra is 7.25 times longer than it is tall.

The fossil of Moganopterus was found at the village of Xiaosanjiazi near Lamadong in Liaoning Province. Moganopterus was named and described in 2012 by Lü Junchang, Pu Hanyong, Xu Li, Wu Yanhua, and Wei Xuefang. The genus name Moganopterus honors the legendary sword couple Gan Jiang and Mo Ye because of its blade-like jaws and includes the Greek word for wing.
The holotype specimen was found in the Barremian-aged Yixian Formation approximately 125 million years ago. The Moganopterus holotype is housed in the Geological Museum of Henan.

Some researchers, such as Longrich, Martill, and Andres (2018), place Moganopterus within the Ctenochasmatidae rather than the Boreopteridae.
